items.excerpt: Diyar Guldogan 29 October 2026• Update: 29 October 2026 WASHINGTON Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Thursday, including Israel’s final vote count, renewed efforts to revive US-Iran talks, Spain mourning one of its deadliest train crashes, North Korea’s missile launches, and Flavio Bolsonaro declaring himself Brazil’s “leader” from the US. More than 500,000 outstanding ballots could reshape Israel’s parliamentary seat distribution as counting continues Thursday, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor its main opposition projected to secure a governing majority. Netanyahu’s bloc was projected to win 53 seats, compared with 48 for the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot and a record combined 19 for predominantly Arab parties, according to Channel 12. A majority requires 61 seats in the 120-member Knesset. The outstanding ballots, cast by soldiers and others voting away from their registered polling stations, were expected to be counted by Thursday evening, Israel’s public broadcaster reported. - Trump confirms Vance’s Iran contact as regional powers push for deal President Donald Trump said Washington is communicating with Iran through mediators, as regional governments seek to revive peace negotiations and avert renewed US strikes. The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei at Trump’s direction. Asked about the contact, Trump said he had approved Vance’s request to help Iran obtain medical supplies. “Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well,” he said. Qatar-led mediators are urging Tehran to allow UN inspectors into bombed nuclear sites in exchange for some US sanctions relief, Axios reported. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Türkiye are supporting the effort. Trump said he did not know whether negotiations would succeed. Trump also had a phone call with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who told him that the Mecca Joint Defense Alliance was closely monitoring developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen. - Spain begins three days of mourning after deadly train crash Spain is in three days of mourning after Wednesday's collision between two high-speed trains killed at least 68 people, one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's recent history. Speaking at the crash site in Toledo, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said authorities would determine the cause of the accident and take action if wrongdoing was uncovered. Sanchez said it was "unacceptable" for a country like Spain to experience two high-speed rail accidents in a single year, referring to January's deadly derailment that claimed the lives of 46 people. "We will get to the bottom of this. If there has been negligence, it will be known," he said, according to Spanish news agency EFE. - Tensions rise as North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles North Korea launched around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan, on Thursday, South Korea’s military said. Seoul stepped up surveillance for further launches and shared information with the US and Japan as officials assessed the missiles’ flight distances and other details, Yonhap News reported. Hours earlier, the Japanese Defense Ministry said Pyongyang had fired "what may be a ballistic missile." That prompted a warning from Japan’s Coast Guard urging ships to avoid any fallen objects, Kyodo News reported. - Flavio Bolsonaro lands in US, declares himself Brazil's leader Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami from Ecuador, despite a court order requiring him to surrender his passports as part of a corruption and money-laundering investigation, according to US media reports. He also published a letter on social media describing himself as the country’s "leader" and vowed to lead the opposition to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva from exile in the US. The son of former President Jair Bolsonaro is under investigation over his alleged links to a banker accused of financial misconduct and a man suspected of money laundering.

items.excerpt: ## Arab Parties Could Determine Next Israeli Prime Minister as Election Produces No Clear Winner Oct 29, 2026 In Israel, Tuesday’s national elections have produced no clear winner, with more than 90% of the votes counted. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party received the most votes, but Netanyahu’s political bloc is likely to fall short of the 61 seats needed to form a government. The leading opposition bloc headed by Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party is projected to win just 48 seats. Israel’s Arab parties are on track to win an unprecedented 19 seats in the Knesset, driven by a surge in turnout by Palestinian citizens of Israel. They are now in a position to help the opposition form a ruling coalition, but it’s unclear if Eisenkot is open to partnering with Palestinian parties. Netanyahu has accused Arab parties of stealing the election, while providing no evidence. This is the leader of the Palestinian-dominated Joint List, Yousef Jabareen. > Yousef Jabareen: “Our power in the Knesset is very decisive, is very crucial. And as we have promised our community, we would like to use this power to facilitate getting rid of Netanyahu’s government and, hopefully, helping to change the political situation in Israel.” ... Alaska’s governor is ordering a criminal investigation into Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola’s campaign, after The New York Times reported that operatives linked to Peltola successfully recruited a second Dan Sullivan to draw votes from Republican Senator Dan Sullivan on the state’s four-person ballot. The effort, called the “ballot composition project” by Peltola’s campaign, reportedly began in the summer of 2025, when campaign aides told a staffer to search voter records for Alaskans named Dan Sullivan. Months later, Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher, announced his candidacy for Senate, switching from unaffiliated to Republican just before the deadline to run. According to the Times, the scheme also involved the Peltola campaign’s lawyers, as well as senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Both Peltola and the DSCC have denied the New York Times report. A former campaign manager told the Times that Peltola was not involved but was definitely aware of the plan.

items.title: PCE inflation report September 2026:
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 8:32 AM EDT Updated 2 Hours Ago Jeff Cox@jeff.cox.7528@JeffCoxCNBCcom Key Points - The U.S. economy grew at a 3.4% pace in the third quarter, faster than expected. - Inflation continued to run above the Fed's 2% target in September, with a headline rate of 3.6% and core at 3.1%, according to the central bank's preferred gauge. - Consumer spending was slightly below forecasts, though still up 0.5%. Personal income increased just 0.2%. ... The pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below. Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends. While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter. GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter. Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%. The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move. "The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday. However, the data deluge from Thursday shows the Fed could have more work to do. A Labor ... Initial jobless claims edged lower to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ended Oct. ... Economic growth has been driven by higher levels of investment from the artificial intelligence build-out, as well as high levels of consumer and government spending. Consumer spending rose 3.8% in the third quarter, the same pace as the prior period. Gross private domestic investment soared 19.4%, driven by a 20.9% surge in equipment spending and an 8.4% jump on intellectual property products. Real sales to private domestic purchasers, a proxy that Fed officials use for underlying demand, rose 4.9%, compared with a 4.6% increase in the second quarter. There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter. September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%. At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

Dan Sullivan, who is running for re-election in a competitive race against Democrat Mary Peltola. ... ## Congressional Democrats ask appropriators to preemptively bar East Potomac Park from being transferred to Trump Congressional Democrats are pushing back on Trump’s efforts to renovate East Potomac Golf Links in Washington. Rep. Jared Huffman, D-Calif., the top Democrat on the House National Resources Committee, today sent a letter to top congressional appropriators, saying a presidential request for $500 million in National Park Services funding to repair its run-down sea wall could be used for construction in East Potomac Park. A Washington judge has repeatedly blocked the administration’s efforts to modify East Potomac Park, after the Justice Department and the president have contradicted each other on whether there are plans in place to construct on the site. Justice Department lawyers last night admitted that there was indeed a plan in place to renovate the park, saying it would close on Nov. 15 to repair the sea wall. Huffman said the funds requested to repair the sea wall could be used to “push the unauthorized golf course project ahead of the long line of NPS’ backlogged maintenance projects across the country.” He further said a legal loophole allows for the interior secretary to “sell NPS land that is ‘no longer needed for public purposes,’ and hand-pick buyers through a private solicitation” — which the congressman said could be used as a loophole to “transfer ownership of East Potomac Park to the President or his allies.” Huffman asked for the appropriators to include language in bills that fund construction in East Potomac Park explicitly bar the sale, exchange or donation of the park to Trump or any of Trump’s relatives or companies. “I support the work necessary to preserve this historic and vital public land. However, it would be unconscionable to let President Trump direct taxpayers to pay for the most expensive portion of the park’s maintenance needs and then take it from them to create a golf course catering to him and his billionaire buddies. Congress must ensure it does not happen,” Huffman wrote. The letter was addressed to Sens. Susan Collins, R-Maine, and Patty Murray, D-Wash., and Reps. Tom Cole, R-Okla., and Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn. Huffman’s proposal would be an uphill battle, as the GOP holds majorities in both chambers — though political winds could shift depending on the outcome of the midterm elections next week. ... items.title: Hegseth reportedly fires military planner; Trump downplays ...
items.excerpt: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has reportedly fired the Pentagon's top military planner amid concerns that Washington may restart strikes on Iran after the midterm elections. Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, according to the Associated Press. No reason was given for his dismissal, and nobody was named as his replacement. Sylvia has now retired, ABC News reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. The AP also reported that U.S. officials have told some countries in the Middle East to be prepared for potential renewed military action against Iran after next week's midterm elections, as well as for any Iranian retaliation. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance had sent a letter to Iran "engaging one of Iran's most powerful hard-liners to revive peace negotiations."
